note: The military careers: Navy ratings, Army military occupational specialties and Air Force specialties whose work five or more skills of the catalogue describe. Each is a career with a service: `service` is the service's key (the employer is the company of data/careers/military/employers.json), `code` the service's code for the job and `codeSystem` the system it is in, `officialTitle` the service's own name for the job and `title` that name with the service in front, because a title is unique and the civilian catalogue has its own Electronics Technician. `home` is a domain of data/skills/taxonomy.json, `what` one sentence, `was` the other names it is found by, `source` the list the code and title were first read from. The words above the name and the tags are derived from the code system and the service (shared/military.ts); the civilian careers a career reaches are computed from the two paths. Every code and title was checked against the Defense Manpower Data Center's occupation file of July 2024, published with O*NET's crosswalk files: `dropped` lists the delivered codes it marks obsolete, and a title that differed was corrected to the file's, the delivered one kept under `was`. Left out on purpose: operators with no maintenance work, IT and cyber, medical other than biomedical equipment, construction trades with no plant equivalent, supply and administration, explosive ordnance disposal and supervisors' codes. The Marine Corps has no careers yet. scripts/build-military-sql.mjs turns this file into a migration (0063); it has no ladder (`leadsTo`): none is curated.
